The Book of Chanokh

CHANOKH

The Book of Parables — Why It Is Excluded

Chapters 37 through 71 in the Traditional Numbering — Not Carried in This Record

An Independent Literary Block Absent From the Dead Sea Scrolls — YHWH’s Name Replaced With a Title — Daniyyel’s Son of Man Inflated Into a Cosmic Judge — The Manipulation Layer Later Mined by Roman-Era Writers

PRIMARY MANUSCRIPT AUTHORITIES

Dead Sea Scrolls — 4QEna (4Q201) · 4QEnastr (4Q208, 4Q209) — Aramaic Primary — the Parables are the sole section absent

Ethiopian Orit Ge’ez — Complete Canon — Primary Witness

YHWH and The Creator only — DSS Attested Sections Only

YHWH / 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and The Creator only — no substitute titles

All personal names in original Hebrew form throughout

THE BOOK OF PARABLES — WHY IT IS EXCLUDED

METHODOLOGY OF THIS RECORD

Physical Verification  Only ancient Chanokh texts used are physically verified on the pre-Christian Aramaic leather of the Dead Sea Scrolls (4Q201, 4Q208, 4Q209).

Pre-Corruption Standard  The later narrative chapters are excluded because their content does not carry the pre-Corruption covenant tradition — the 364-day solar calendar, the covenant memory, and YHWH as the unsubstituted name. A text’s standing rests on the tradition it preserves, never on a dating imposed on it.

Linguistic Independence  The Ge’ez Orit is used to analyze the creation and legal frameworks because its Semitic grammar preserves the feminine Ruach and the legal office of ha-satan, completely exposing late Western theological alterations.

WHY THESE CHAPTERS ARE EXCLUDED

[CRITICAL NOTE]  The Book of Parables is an independent literary block that was dropped into the middle of the Chanokh corpus long after the Dead Sea Scrolls were archived. These chapters do not appear in any Dead Sea Scrolls manuscript — the only section of the entire Book of Chanokh missing from the ancient record.

[CRITICAL NOTE]  Within these chapters, YHWH’s name is systematically erased and replaced with the title “Lord of Spirits” over one hundred times. The original pre-Rabbinic, pre-Christian covenant texts do not contain this substitution. This is a scribal alteration of the divine name, not original covenant language.

[CRITICAL NOTE]  These chapters also take the phrase “one like a son of man” from a vision in the Book of Daniyyel — a human figure in a prophetic dream — and inflate it into a cosmic heavenly judge hidden since before creation. That is not what Daniyyel’s text says. It is scribal invention: a new theological construct built by expanding a single covenant image beyond anything the original text described.

[CRITICAL NOTE]  Roman-era NT writers then mined this scribal construction — not the original covenant texts — to assemble their invented deity. The manipulation trail runs from the scribal additions in these chapters directly into the NT’s fabricated claims. These chapters are the manipulation layer. They are excluded from this record because they document what Second Temple scribes invented, not what the original covenant tradition preserved.

The following chapters — renumbered from their original Ge’ez Orit position — return to the pre-Second Temple, pre-Christian, pre-Rabbinic primary text.
